notes.subject: canary directory-bind
notes.text: not rendered: the environment is an Assured Workloads workload (FEDRAMP_MODERATE), where Google supports neither uptime checks nor synthetic monitors (their requests may come from any uptime region)
how: Run the same check from inside the boundary: a scheduled job on the environment's own compute (a Kubernetes CronJob, or a timer on a server) running the probe, its result written as a Cloud Monitoring custom metric with an alert policy on it
Or alert on what the products log: log-based alert policies on failed sign-ins, LDAP binds or SAML errors
Or run the check from a monitoring project outside the Assured Workloads folder, only if the authorizing official accepts check requests and results crossing the boundary
notes.scope: ldap-bind check of ds-ldaps-service in standby/prod; alert rule login-failures goes without it

notes.subject: Assured Workloads (FEDRAMP_MODERATE)
notes.text: Cloud Logging, Compute Engine and GKE are supported products; the Ops Agent isn't listed on its own, and restrictions on log sinks and GKE workload logging under it are to be confirmed
how: Ask Google's account team whether the Ops Agent, log sinks and GKE workload logging may be used under the workload's compliance regime before relying on them

notes.subject: Elastic Agent on role pf-admin
notes.text: its servers' log files reach the Elastic data streams through the Fleet agent policy opsdir-standby-prod-pf-admin (rendered); enrolling the servers is the Elastic team's, and the Fleet Server URL and the policy's enrollment token are Fleet's, never rendered
how: Install Elastic Agent on pf-admin-1 enrolled in opsdir-standby-prod-pf-admin: elastic-agent install --url <Fleet Server URL> --enrollment-token <its enrollment token>
Applying the API documents: install the filestream integration package 2.5.1 first (POST /api/fleet/epm/packages/filestream/2.5.1); the Terraform installs it

notes.subject: Elastic Agent on role pf-engine
notes.text: its servers' log files reach the Elastic data streams through the Fleet agent policy opsdir-standby-prod-pf-engine (rendered); enrolling the servers is the Elastic team's, and the Fleet Server URL and the policy's enrollment token are Fleet's, never rendered
how: Install Elastic Agent on pf-engine-1, pf-engine-2 enrolled in opsdir-standby-prod-pf-engine: elastic-agent install --url <Fleet Server URL> --enrollment-token <its enrollment token>
Applying the API documents: install the filestream integration package 2.5.1 first (POST /api/fleet/epm/packages/filestream/2.5.1); the Terraform installs it

notes.subject: Elastic data stream logs-ciam.security-standby
notes.text: opsdir-logs-ciam.security-standby is attached through the component template logs-ciam.security@custom, which takes effect for the backing indices created from the next rollover, and only where the stream's index template composes it (Fleet integration templates do; the built-in logs template doesn't)
how: Switch the existing backing indices: remove their policy, then PUT logs-ciam.security-standby/_settings with index.lifecycle.name opsdir-logs-ciam.security-standby
Confirm the stream's index template composes logs-ciam.security@custom, and that nothing else the Elastic team keeps in that component template is lost (opsdir writes all of it)

notes.subject: Ops Agent configuration
notes.text: opsdir renders it for configuration management to place (/etc/google-cloud-ops-agent/config.yaml); it replaces one the servers already have (the agent reads only that file): merge their own receivers and pipelines into it; the agent itself comes with the host baseline
how: Before configuration management places /etc/google-cloud-ops-agent/config.yaml, merge the receivers and pipelines of the servers' own file into it, by hand

notes.subject: Elastic rule actions
